sources.title: Christina Brandt and Patrick Horn, Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems, arXiv:2610.13483v1
sources.locator: Complete 22-page v1 paper; all named results inspected. Core locations: §2.1 Theorem 1 (pp. 2–3); §2.2 Theorems 2, 4, 6 and Assumption 5 (pp. 3–9); §3 Theorem 9 and Example 1 (pp. 11–16); conclusion §4 (p. 17); Appendix A Theorems 10–14 and Lemma 12 (pp. 20–21); Appendix B Theorems 15–16 (pp. 21–22).

contents.name: Abstract/introduction order convention: abstract says A=F o G while the body uses A=G o F and estimator R_F R_G
Theorem 1 and complete proof: composition regularizes the compatible minimum-norm factorization
Theorem 2: generic source-ball minimax lower bound for one regularization
contents.reason: This lower bound concerns a general single operator and does not supply a matching lower bound for the two-stage composite discrepancy rule.

contents.name: Remark 3: a priori two-stage parameter balance
contents.reason: The assigned theorem concerns the a posteriori double-discrepancy rules; the separate a priori rate is outside this page's claim.

contents.name: Theorem 4: ordinary one-operator Morozov qualification result
Theorem 6 and complete proof: double-discrepancy residual rules and conditional rate
Lemma 7: spectral formula and bounds for the second residual operator
Lemma 8: source-multiplier identity for the composite bias
Theorem 9: Fourier-slice reconstruction formula for the Radon transform
contents.reason: This tomography formula is an application section and supplies no hypothesis or proof step for the composite Hilbert-space DDP theorem.

contents.name: Example 1: convolution experiment and numerical DDP behavior
contents.reason: The numerical convolution experiment is not a proof or boundary case for this page; the assigned B leaves are separate finite matrix examples.

contents.name: Theorem 10: Picard condition for the composite operator
contents.reason: The authored theorem assumes an exact source element and proves the needed minimum-norm compatibility from its common system without invoking this range criterion.

contents.name: Theorem 11: interpolation inequality
Lemma 12: spectral-filter operator-norm bound
Theorem 13: Fourier-slice theorem
contents.reason: The Radon-transform Fourier identity is outside the assigned factorized inverse-operator claims.

contents.name: Theorem 14: singular system of the disk Radon transform
contents.reason: This application-specific Radon singular system is not used by the common abstract singular-system theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 15: functional calculus for self-adjoint operators
contents.reason: The convolution appendix functional calculus is not needed; the theorem states its compact spectral-filter assumptions explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 16: Fourier representation of convolution functional calculus
contents.reason: This convolution representation supports the numerical application only and is not used in the assigned theorem or examples.

contents.name: Theorem 6 statement/proof discrepancy: z is typed as |A|^nu w and the displayed rho exponent does not follow from equation (20)
Conclusion §4: explicit a-priori optimality question and separate finite-qualification DDP rate; DDP sharpness is the local item's own question
